solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tussore worked with gold for the bottom drawer (9)

indicatorNotes.worked: fabric that has been worked is reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Someone sews silk and gold thread into linen to save for a wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is British for the linen and household goods a bride-to-be collects before marriage, the American hope chest; tussore is a coarse silk.
annotation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the bride's collection of clothes and linen, just what the bottom drawer holds.

entries.clue: Exhausted Member of the Dail broken by Ireland (5)

indicatorNotes.broken by: TD is split open and IRE sits in the break

blocks.note: a TD (Teachta Dála) is a member of the Irish parliament
Ire is the Irish name for Ireland

annotation.surface: An Irish politician is worn out by the country he serves.
annotation.walkthrough: TD is the Irish equivalent of MP: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
annotation.definitionFit: Tired and exhausted both mean worn out.

entries.clue: Company set up a lot of ongoing church event (10)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up lifts the letters so they read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the word, not all of it: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A firm organises most of a parish's continuing activities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Church event' looks like one phrase, but church is only CE; the definition is the last word alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything that happens or takes place counts as both.

entries.clue: Measure introduced by country, spreading from the centre (8)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: the country takes the measure inside itself

blocks.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

annotation.surface: A nation brings in a policy that radiates outwards from the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like a law a country passes; it is an old unit of cloth length, about 45 inches.
annotation.definitionFit: Stellate means star-shaped, with points radiating from a centre.

entries.clue: Order used in some dictionaries (5)

blocks.note: an electronic dictionary, e- for electronic plus the usual short form of dictionary

annotation.surface: An instruction about which reference books to consult.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: an e-dict is an electronic dictionary, so EDICT is the form some dictionaries come in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a proclamation issued by a ruler commands obedience.

entries.clue: Uncover second butterfly in centre of sand hills (9)

indicatorNotes.centre of: keep only the middle of the word

blocks.note: DUNES without its first and last letters; split around the insert
the heath is a family of small brown butterflies

annotation.surface: A second butterfly is spotted among the dunes, flushed out of hiding.
annotation.walkthrough: The heath butterflies, small heath and large heath, are named for the moorland they live on, which suits the sand-hill surface.
annotation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a blade is to draw it from its cover, so to uncover it.

entries.clue: Unlit playing area has defender crossing line (5-5)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the defender reaches across the line, holding it inside

blocks.note: a back is a defensive player

annotation.surface: A floodlight failure on the football field while a defender steps over a line.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture makes 'line' a touchline; it is just L, the standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Pitch-black means completely dark, with no light at all.

entries.clue: Be very nosy about closure of stone quarry (4)

indicatorNotes.closure of: the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy

annotation.surface: Someone snooping around the shutting down of a stone quarry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone quarry' reads as one place, but quarry is the definition: the hunted animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Quarry is an animal being hunted, which is prey.

entries.clue: Beginning to turn fish catcher’s reel (6)

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: take the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: An angler starts winding in the reel.
annotation.walkthrough: The fishing scene makes 'reel' a noun on a rod; it is the verb, to stagger.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe walking unsteadily, like someone dizzy or drunk.

entries.clue: One often on the job in bed? (14)

annotation.definition: One often on the job in bed?

blocks.note: reads as a sexual euphemism; really someone at work
reads as the bedroom; really a flower bed

annotation.surface: A saucy hint about someone busy in the bedroom.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, where a gardener spends working hours.
annotation.definitionFit: A horticulturist is a gardener, who works in flower beds.

entries.clue: Having abandoned property plot located round Old Street (4-3-5)

indicatorNotes.round: LAND goes round the old street

annotation.surface: A deserted property on a plot near Old Street, the London road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Located' is placed last in the answer though it sits before 'round' in the clue. A lost-and-found office holds items people have left behind.
annotation.definitionFit: A lost-and-found office is defined by holding abandoned property.

entries.clue: Crack core voice, withdrawing over and over again (7)

indicatorNotes.withdrawing: the O is taken out of each word

blocks.clueFragment: voice, withdrawing over and over again
blocks.note: VOICE with O removed, the second time

annotation.surface: A central voice drops out of the choir, time after time.
annotation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is O in crosswords; 'over and over again' says take one O out of each of the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrow opening or fissure in rock or a wall.

entries.clue: Drive rig with energy (3-2-3-2)

blocks.note: a get-up or rig is an outfit
go = energy, as in full of go

annotation.surface: Driving a lorry, or a rig, with plenty of power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'rig' pull toward trucks; drive is the noun for ambition, and a rig is a costume.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for energetic ambition, the noun sense of drive, as in someone lacking motivation.

entries.clue: Hear wrongly about account — key problem for the listener? (7)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: the letters are set down in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go round the account

blocks.note: HEAR rearranged, split to take AC

annotation.surface: Mishearing a bank statement, then asking whether the problem is a stuck key.
annotation.walkthrough: The listener is anyone with ears, and the question mark flags the play on the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, a problem for anyone listening.

entries.clue: Officer, one sometimes preceding general (9)

blocks.note: an official whose title is completed by the word 'General'

annotation.surface: An army officer who comes before a general in rank.
annotation.walkthrough: The ranks picture suggests someone below a general; the wording means the word placed before 'general', as in Inspector General.
annotation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police officer, and the title Inspector General puts it before 'general'.

entries.clue: Glasses with bits of dust detected (5)

indicatorNotes.detected: picked up by the ear rather than seen written down

annotation.surface: Spectacles on which some dust has been noticed.
annotation.walkthrough: Specks and specs are said the same way; one is the dust you see on the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British shortening of spectacles, worn to correct eyesight.

entries.clue: Source of radiation is up — it’s a problem for airways (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the sun radiates light and heat
it's written out in full: IT IS

annotation.surface: A radiation leak is under way, bad news for the airline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Airways' looks like airlines; it means the breathing passages.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses, which blocks the airways of the nose.

entries.clue: Dresses too little for what they cover (12)

blocks.note: under- = too little, as in underpaid

annotation.surface: A complaint that some dresses are too skimpy for what they are meant to cover.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, 'dresses too little' is under-clothes; read as a noun, dresses are what cover the underclothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: a frock is worn on top of vests, slips and knickers, hiding them.

entries.clue: Thought: the settling of disputes is about time (10)

indicatorNotes.is about: the settling word goes round the time

annotation.surface: A reflection that resolving arguments is mostly a matter of time.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon makes this sound like a proverb; 'Thought' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deep, quiet contemplation of an idea is serious thinking.

entries.clue: User of rack perhaps right to be fitted in large open-top car (8)

indicatorNotes.to be fitted in: a part fitted in a car is installed inside it, so RT goes within TOURER

blocks.note: a tourer is a large open car

annotation.surface: Someone with a roof rack wants it fitted to a big convertible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rack' belongs on a car roof in this picture; it is the medieval torture device that stretched victims.
annotation.definitionFit: The rack was an instrument of torture, so one using it is a torturer.

entries.clue: A university citation then redrafted a task for a notary (14)

indicatorNotes.redrafted: a redrafted text is rewritten, so the letters are reordered

annotation.surface: A university reference is rewritten, the kind of job a notary handles.
annotation.walkthrough: A notary is a lawyer who certifies documents and signatures as genuine.
annotation.definitionFit: Authenticating documents, confirming they are genuine, is a notary's job.

entries.clue: Name a good insect for shrew (9)

blocks.note: a term is a name for something

annotation.surface: Naming a helpful bug that feeds a small mammal.
annotation.walkthrough: The insect picture makes shrew the small animal; it is a bad-tempered woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, a shrew.

entries.clue: Meeting one against Liszt, perhaps English (10)

blocks.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
Ferenc is the Hungarian first name of the composer Franz Liszt

annotation.surface: A meeting where one person objects to Liszt, possibly an Englishman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liszt, perhaps' asks for something Liszt is an example of: a man called Ferenc.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a formal gathering where people discuss business.

entries.clue: Attila perhaps reportedly fears veteran divisions (8)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Attila was king of the Huns

annotation.surface: Attila, by all accounts, is afraid of battle-hardened army units.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Veteran divisions' pictures army units; veteran just means old, and a hundred was an old subdivision of an English county.
annotation.definitionFit: Hundreds were historic administrative divisions of English counties.

entries.clue: Exercises with a small warning such as might get child puffing? (10)

annotation.definition: such as might get child puffing?

blocks.note: a hooter is a horn or siren that sounds a warning

annotation.surface: Gym class with a gentle alert, as might leave a child out of breath.
annotation.walkthrough: Puffing seems to mean breathless after exercise; the child is blowing through a tube.
annotation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube a child blows peas through.

entries.clue: Appalling court order (6)

annotation.surface: A shocking ruling from the bench.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court order' reads as one legal phrase; court is only CT and order is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: a boss can instruct or command staff.

entries.clue: Getting into stocks for one in official garment (10)

blocks.note: a vestment is a ceremonial robe

annotation.surface: Someone climbs into medieval stocks while dressed in ceremonial robes.
annotation.walkthrough: The stocks look like the wooden punishment frame; they are shares on the market.
annotation.definitionFit: Buying stocks and shares is one example of investment.

entries.clue: Nothing once purchased loses billions (5)

indicatorNotes.loses: whatever a word loses is no longer part of it, so B comes off BOUGHT

annotation.surface: Something once bought for a fortune is now worth nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an old word: ought, like aught, used to mean nought.
annotation.definitionFit: Ought is an archaic variant of nought, meaning nothing.

entries.clue: Parade of geese irregularly chased by returning doggy? (5-4)

indicatorNotes.chased by: what chases comes behind, so the dog follows the geese
indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: geese is the irregular plural of goose; the regular one would be gooses

annotation.surface: A flock of geese is chased by a dog running back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irregularly' suggests alternate letters, but it points at grammar: geese is the irregular form of what would regularly be GOOSES.
annotation.definitionFit: To goose-step is to march stiff-legged on parade.

entries.clue: Heron with tail and tibia broken gets healing treatment (14)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters are broken apart and reassembled

annotation.surface: An injured heron with a damaged tail and leg bone receives vet care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'and' only join the three fodder words.
annotation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation is treatment to restore health after injury.

entries.clue: Love? Halo? These in essence may appear so (4)

annotation.definition: Love? Halo? These in essence may appear so

indicatorNotes.in essence: the essence is the heart, so take the middle letters

annotation.surface: A musing on whether love and a halo look alike at heart.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: love is 0 in tennis, and a halo is a ring, both round shapes.
annotation.definitionFit: The letter O (love) and a halo are both oval shapes.

entries.clue: What may track down renegade changing sides in fight? (8)

indicatorNotes.changing sides in: one side letter of fight swaps for the other

blocks.note: the sides of FighT are F and T; F becomes T

annotation.surface: Hunting a traitor who switched allegiance during a battle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's changing sides means betrayal; here it is the two outside letters of fight, F out and T in.
annotation.definitionFit: A detector is a device that tracks down things, such as metal.

entries.clue: Metal satellite — one with edges of Uranium (8)

blocks.note: first and last letters of UraniuM

annotation.surface: A metal moon orbiting close to the planet Uranus.
annotation.walkthrough: Uranium looks like a second metal here; it only donates its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the element Ti is a strong, light, silvery transition element.

entries.clue: To us, nurse is working hard (9)

indicatorNotes.is working: the letters are put to work in a new order

annotation.surface: A patient remarks that the nurse is working really hard.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'working hard' as a phrase; 'hard' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Strenuous means demanding great effort, hard.

entries.clue: Changing environment sounded alarm for old Chinese rulers (12)

indicatorNotes.sounded: spoken, so what is heard counts

annotation.surface: An alarm is raised for the old emperors of China.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sounded alarm' looks like raising an alarm; it asks for a word that sounds like terror.
annotation.definitionFit: A science-fiction term for reshaping another planet's climate and surface so humans could live there.

entries.clue: No longer watch out after second run for free program (9)

indicatorNotes.after: the watch-out word comes after the others

blocks.note: to hare is to run fast
ware! is an old warning, beware

annotation.surface: An old warning about a second free run of some software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No longer' tells you WARE is archaic, not that anything is removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Shareware is software distributed free, at least for a trial.

entries.clue: Young one succeeded with expedition over heather (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over puts these letters above the heather

annotation.surface: A youngster makes it on an expedition across the moors.
annotation.walkthrough: Ling is the standard crossword heather.
annotation.definitionFit: A somewhat literary word for a lad or youth not yet fully grown.

entries.clue: Gold found in dry French river, a slow runner (8)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so OR sits within TT

blocks.note: the Oise, a tributary of the Seine

annotation.surface: Gold turns up in the dry bed of a French river, where a slow creature crawls.
annotation.walkthrough: The runner is the tortoise of the fable that races the hare.
annotation.definitionFit: The tortoise is proverbially slow, the loser-turned-winner of Aesop's race.

entries.clue: Laze about? This can get one fired (4)

annotation.surface: Lazing around at work is the sort of thing that gets you sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: Fired seems to mean sacked, which laziness would earn; it means fired up with enthusiasm.
annotation.definitionFit: Fired here means fired up: eager enthusiasm or fervour is what inspires a person.

entries.clue: Letters illuminated with tare and rue interwoven (10)

indicatorNotes.interwoven: the letters are woven into a new order

annotation.surface: A decorated manuscript with weeds and herbs woven into its borders.
annotation.walkthrough: Tare is a weed and rue a herb, which fit illuminated letters; 'Letters' means learning, as in a man of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Letters in the sense of literary culture means literature.

entries.clue: Repeat cure afresh and get better (10)

indicatorNotes.afresh: the letters are laid out anew

annotation.surface: A patient takes the treatment again and recovers.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface is close to the answer's own meaning, which makes the anagram easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to recover health after illness or injury.

entries.clue: Turner starts on representation of rocky hill (5)

indicatorNotes.starts on: take the starting letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

annotation.surface: J M W Turner begins a painting of a craggy hill.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter; it is anything that turns.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotor is the turning part of a machine.

entries.clue: Commit to fire one new film judge (10)

annotation.surface: A critic consigns a new film to the flames.
annotation.walkthrough: The film-review picture suits the answer, which is what makes the breakdown into four pieces easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to burn something completely, reducing it to ash.

entries.clue: Rate of SA currency holding record edge (9)

indicatorNotes.holding: the currency holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A question about the exchange rate of the South African rand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rate of SA currency' reads as an exchange rate; rate is an old verb meaning to scold.
annotation.definitionFit: To rate someone, in older English, is to berate or reprimand them.

entries.clue: Collection including extinct group (6)

annotation.surface: A museum collection that includes some vanished species.
annotation.walkthrough: EXT is the dictionary abbreviation for extinct.
annotation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, usually musicians.

entries.clue: Private medics to get new deal (8)

indicatorNotes.new deal: the letters are dealt out again like cards

annotation.surface: Doctors in private practice are to get a new contract.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Private medics' reads as one phrase about private healthcare; Private is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Domestic means to do with home and family life, private.

entries.clue: Act decently in drama festival (4,4)

annotation.surface: Performing respectably at a theatre festival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Act' pairs with drama in the surface; here it just means behave.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from sport: to follow the rules honestly and treat others justly.

entries.clue: Collector of rubbish street cleaner at first missed. Peel, perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Street Cleaner; dropped

annotation.surface: A binman's first sweep along the street missed a potato peel.
annotation.walkthrough: Peel is Emma Peel, secret agent in the 1960s British TV series The Avengers, not potato skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Emma Peel, played by Diana Rigg, was a secret agent in that television series.

entries.clue: Jumbo next to jumbo, very close together (6-2-6)

blocks.note: bumper = extra large, as in a bumper crop

annotation.surface: Two elephants stand side by side, squeezed together.
annotation.walkthrough: In a Times Jumbo puzzle, 'Jumbo' also winks at the crossword itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Bumper-to-bumper describes traffic packed very close together.

entries.clue: Rue not seeing later king about name for the future George IV (6)

indicatorNotes.not seeing: the letter is left out of sight
indicatorNotes.about: the shortened word goes round N

blocks.note: R = rex, king; the later of REGRET's two Rs goes, leaving REGET

annotation.surface: A later monarch refuses to regret choosing a name for the prince.
annotation.walkthrough: The future George IV ruled as Prince Regent from 1811 while George III was ill.
annotation.definitionFit: Before becoming king, George IV was the Prince Regent.

entries.clue: What’s useful for getting into cold sheets? (10)

annotation.definition: What’s useful for getting into cold sheets?

blocks.note: reads as help climbing into bed; really forcing a passage through
reads as chilly bedding; really frozen sheets of sea ice

annotation.surface: Advice for sliding into a chilly bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The cold sheets are ice sheets at sea, which an icebreaker ship cuts through.
annotation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a ship built to force a way through sheet ice.

entries.clue: Part of pop song put round with ‘The Boxer’, perhaps? (12)

indicatorNotes.put round: the song part goes round the letter

blocks.note: the middle eight is a contrasting section of a pop song

annotation.surface: A section of a pop song set around Simon and Garfunkel's 'The Boxer'.
annotation.walkthrough: The Boxer is a Simon and Garfunkel song, which fits the pop surface; the definition takes it as a fighter, perhaps in that weight class.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a fighter in the weight class between welter and light-heavy.

entries.clue: Prevent wild animals eating them, destroying the border (5)

indicatorNotes.eating: the animals take the letter inside
indicatorNotes.destroying: the border is removed from them

annotation.surface: Stopping deer from eating the plants and ruining the flower border.
annotation.walkthrough: The border sounds like a garden bed; it is a hem, taken out of THEM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discouraging someone from acting stops the act happening.

entries.clue: Outfit with, initially, geese, emus and sheep (3-2)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: A farm kitted out with geese, emus and sheep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' covers only geese and emus; TUP, a British word for a ram, is the whole sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym for a costume or set of clothes, often an eccentric one.

entries.clue: Bring up the tail end (4)

annotation.surface: Bringing up the back of a line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bring up the rear' is the phrase the clue imitates, and the two senses are the verb (raise a child) and the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb it means raising children or livestock; as a noun it means the back part.

entries.clue: Italian tenor, large one closing live performance (5)

indicatorNotes.closing: these letters come at the close of the other word

blocks.note: a gig is a live show

annotation.surface: A big Italian tenor brings the concert to an end.
annotation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was a famous Italian operatic tenor of the early 20th century.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated operatic singer from Recanati.

entries.clue: Awkward lines with elegy — Dante to remove outer parts (9)

indicatorNotes.to remove outer parts: strip each word of its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Clumsy verse in a lament, so Dante sets about cutting it.
annotation.walkthrough: The instruction applies to all three words, not just Dante.
annotation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, awkward.

entries.clue: Men led by characteristic backstabber (7)

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: Soldiers under a commander known for betrayal.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a troop and its leader; the soldiers come second.
annotation.definitionFit: A traitor stabs others in the back.

entries.clue: Programme editor dropping duke in favour of knight’s forebear (10)

indicatorNotes.dropping: to drop someone is to leave them out, so the duke's D goes
indicatorNotes.in favour of: choosing one in favour of another means replacing it, so N takes D's place

blocks.note: N is the knight in chess notation; replaces D

annotation.surface: A TV editor sidelines a duke in favour of a knight's ancestor.
annotation.walkthrough: Knight is N, not K: in chess notation K is already the king.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an ancestor from whom a family line descends.

entries.clue: Trade chip circuits at a very low price (4-5)

indicatorNotes.circuits: the letters go round and come out in a new order

annotation.surface: Microchip circuit boards are being traded for next to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chip' and 'circuits' make an electronics picture; circuits is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Dirt-cheap means extremely inexpensive.
